aaroh: S R G M P D N S'
avaroh: S' N D P M G R S

shuddh: all — Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni

notes_used: All shuddh (natural) swaras — Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni. No komal, no teevra. Ma is present in both aaroh and avaroh.
characteristic_pakad: G M P D N S'
emotional_resonance: confusion and mental fog in the morning
stress from a bad night's sleep
lack of motivation to start work
therapy_note: Bilawal uses all natural swaras — there is no tension or darkness in this raag. It sounds clear, bright and open, like sunlight entering a room. Practicing it in the morning resets the nervous system, brings clarity of thought, and creates a calm foundation for the day. It is the musical equivalent of a deep breath and a fresh start.

bollywood_references.title: Bhor Bhai Din Chad Gaya
bollywood_references.note: Contains Bilawal characteristics in its morning freshness — not a strict classical treatment

classical_references.type: Vocal — recordings considered the high standard for Bilawal

notes_for_vocalist: All swaras are shuddh — including Ma, which must appear in both aaroh and avaroh (a previous version of this file omitted Ma from the aaroh, which was an error). Ga and Dha are the vadi and samvadi — they carry the most expression. Ni shuddh gives the raag its bright, open character. Avoid heavy use of lower register — this raag lives in the middle and upper octaves.
common_mistakes: Omitting Ma from the aaroh — Ma is present in both directions
Accidentally using komal Ni — all notes are shuddh
Making it sound like Yaman by over-emphasising the Ma-Ga movement without the teevra Ma distinction
variant_notes: Bilawal is also the name of a thaat (parent scale). The raag Bilawal uses Ma more sparingly than the full thaat implies — Ma has alpatva (weak note) status in some treatments.
